title: NavigationStack: paths, sheets and full-screen covers

videos.script: Tap a course, and its screen slides in over the list. Tap back, and it slides away. That is a stack, and this lesson is about who owns it. {{stack}} NavigationStack goes once, at the root. {{values}} Links push a value, not a view. A route that names a course by its id. One modifier decides which screen shows a route. {{path}} Then the stack becomes an array you own. A tap appends. Back removes the last element. Code can jump anywhere with one assignment. {{save}} So the array can be saved. You encode it to JSON, read it back, and check it against the plan. A screen for a deleted session is dropped, not shown empty. {{links}} A link from outside the app becomes a path too. It is input, so it is parsed strictly, and tests say what it refuses. {{sheets}} Then the screens that are not part of the stack. A sheet, for adding a session. A full-screen cover, for a timer. {{choice}} And one question that picks between them. What should back do?
